title: Multiplexed proteomic profiling of cysteine reactivity and ligandability in human T cells
protocol: Thaw cell pellets on ice.
Resuspend cells in cold PBS (550–600 μL).
Lysate by sonication (2 × 8 pulses, 40% duty cycle, output setting = 4).
Normalize protein concentration to 1.5–2.0 mg/mL using a standard DC protein assay.
Optional: Separate soluble and particulate proteomic fractions by ultracentrifugation (100,000 g, 45 min).
Optional: Treat total proteome or fractions with scout fragments KB02 or KB05 (500 μM final concentration) for 1 h at ambient temperature.
Treat proteomes (500 μL, 1.5–2.0 mg/mL) with IA-DTB (100 μM final concentration) for 1 h at ambient temperature.
Add ice-cold methanol (600 μL), chloroform (100 μL), and water (100 μL).
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Centrifuge the mixture (10,000 g, 10 min, 4°C) to form a protein disc at the interface of chloroform and aqueous layers.
Aspirate both layers without disturbing the protein disc.
Aspirate just the top layer if the disk does not form properly.
Add cold methanol (1 mL) to the disk and vortex.
Pellet the proteins (10,000 g, 10 min, 4°C).
Re-suspend the resulting pellets in 90 μL of buffer containing 9M urea, 10 mM DTT, and 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate by thorough pipetting up and down or sonication.
Heat the resulting mixture at 65°C for 20 min.
Cool the sample to room temperature.
Add iodoacetamide (10 μL of 500 mM solution in H2O) and incubate the samples in the dark at 37°C for 30 min with shaking.
Dilute the samples with 305 μL of Buffer A (TEAB buffer, 50 mM, pH 8.5).
Add trypsin (4 μL of 0.25 μg/μL trypsin in trypsin buffer containing 25 mM CaCl2) and digest the proteins at 37°C for 2 h.
Incubate the tryptic digest step overnight at 37°C with agitation.
Dilute the samples with 400 μL of wash buffer (50 mM TEAB, pH 8.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.2% NP-40).
Add 50 μL of streptavidin-agarose beads to each sample.
Rotate the bead mixture for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash streptavidin-agarose bead slurry in 2× wash buffer (1 mL) twice and bring up to initial volume with 2× wash buffer for a 10-plex sample.
Pellet the beads by centrifugation at 2,000 g for 1 min.
Transfer the beads to BioSpin columns.
Wash the beads three times each with 1 mL of wash buffer, PBS, and H2O.
Elute peptides by adding 300 μL of 50% aqueous CH3CN containing 0.1% formic acid.
Evaporate the eluate to dryness using a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Re-suspend the peptides in 100 μL Buffer B (200 mM EPPS, pH 8.0 with 30% CH3CN).
Vortex and spin down the re-suspended peptides at 2,000 g for 1 min.
Add TMT tags to corresponding tubes and allow the reaction to proceed for 60 minutes.
Quench the reaction by adding 5% hydroxylamine (3 μL per sample).
Vortex the samples.
Spin down the tubes.
Leave the samples at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Add FA (5 μL, final concentration: 5% v/v) to each tube.
Vortex the tubes again.
Spin down the tubes once more.
Combine all labeled channels in a single low binding 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Dry the final combined sample using a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Store the dry sample at −80°C until desalting and high pH fractionation.
Re-suspend the samples in solvent A (1 mL, 95% H2O, 5% CH3CN, 0.1% FA).
Acidify with 20 μL of 20% FA in H2O.
Pass through Sep-Pak C18 cartridges to desalt and fractionate the sample.
Condition the cartridge with CH3CN (3 × 1 mL).
Equilibrate the cartridge with solvent A (3 × 1 mL).
Load the sample by dropwise addition.
Wash the cartridge with the flow-through from the sample (1 × 0.5 mL).
Desalt by passing solvent A (3 × 1 mL).
Elute the peptides by adding 1 mL of solvent B (80% CH3CN, 20% H2O, 0.1% FA).
Evaporate the eluent to dryness using SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Resuspend the sample in solvent A (500 μL) with sonication.
Fractionate the sample into a 96 deep-well plate using HPLC (Agilent).
Add 20 μL of 20% FA to each well in a 96-well collection plate to acidify the eluting peptides.
Elute peptides onto a capillary column (ZORBAX 300Extend-C18, 75 μm).
Separate peptides using a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min with the specified gradient.
Collect fractions from 5 to 75 minutes in 96-well plates according to collection mode A1-A12, B1-B12, C1-C12, D1-D12, E1-E12, F1-F12, G1-G12, H1-H12.
Evaporate eluent to dryness in the plate using a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Re-suspend peptides in solvent B (80% CH3CN, 20% H2O, 0.1% FA; 75 μL/well).
Combine all wells from each column into new clean Eppendorf tubes (Columns 1–12 become fractions f1–f12), resulting in 12 total fractions.
Wash the wells with solvent B (80% CH3CN, 20% H2O, 0.1% FA; 200 μL/column) and repeat the washing process for each row of wells.
Remove solvent using SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Store samples at -80°C for mass-spectrometry analysis.
Re-suspend the resulting 12 combined fractions in solvent A.
Analyze the samples on the Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer.
Inject the sample using an UltiMate 3000 Series Rapid Separation LC system and autosampler.
Elute peptides onto a capillary column packed with C18 (Waters, Acquity BEH C18, 1.7 μm, 25 cm).
Separate peptides at a flow rate of 0.25 μL/min using the specified gradient conditions.
Apply a voltage of 1.9 kV to the nano-LC electrospray ionization source during analysis.
Begin the scan sequence with an MS1 master scan in Orbitrap analysis, resolution 120,000, 400−1700 m/z, RF lens 60%, automatic gain control target 2E5, maximum injection time 50 ms, centroid mode.
Enable dynamic exclusion (repeat count 1, duration 15 s).
Select the top ten precursors for MS2/MS3 analysis.

Isolate quadrupole precursor ions with an isolation window of 0.7 and perform collision-induced dissociation in the ion trap at AGC 1.8E4, normalized collision energy 35%, maximum injection time 120 ms.
Enable synchronous precursor selection to select up to 10 MS2 fragment ions for MS3 analysis.
Fragment MS3 precursors by higher-energy collisional dissociation and analyze using Orbitrap at collision energy 55%, AGC 1.5E5, maximum injection time 120 ms, resolution 50,000.
Use charge state–dependent isolation windows for MS3 analysis: set the window to 1.2 for charge state z = 2 and to 0.7 for charge states z = 3-6.
Extract MS2 and MS3 files from raw files using RAW Converter version 1.1.0.22.
Upload extracted files to Integrated Proteomics Pipeline (IP2).
Search uploaded data using ProLuCID algorithm with a reverse concatenated, non-redundant variant of the Human UniProt database (release-2012_11).
Modify cysteine residues for carboxyamidomethylation (+57.02146 Da) and allow up to one differential modification for desthiobiotin tag (+398.2529 Da).
Modify N-termini and lysine residues with a static modification corresponding to the TMT tag (+229.1629 Da).
Select trypsin as the enzyme of choice.
Require peptides to be at least 6 amino acids long, have at least one tryptic terminus, and contain the DTB modification.
Filter ProLuCID data through DTASelect (version 2.0) to achieve a peptide false-positive rate below 1%.
Perform the MS3-based peptide quantification with reporter ion mass tolerance set to 20 ppm using Integrated Proteomics Pipeline (IP2).
